title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi inoculation effects on crop yield
research_question: Does inoculation with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) increase crop yield, and how does the effect vary by crop type and P availability?

population.description: Crop plants inoculated with AMF in field or greenhouse experiments

comparator.definition: Plants grown without mycorrhizal inoculum, or with sterilized inoculum

primary.unit: g/plant, kg/ha, Mg/ha, or relative to control

control: Non-inoculated control (no AMF or sterilized inoculum)
primary_outcomes: Plant biomass or crop yield (shoot dry weight, grain yield, total biomass)
typical_effect_size: +23% plant biomass (range +10% to +50% depending on P availability)
important_moderators: Crop species or functional group (C3 grass, C4 grass, legume, non-legume forb)
AMF species or genus (Glomus, Rhizophagus, mixed inoculum)
Phosphorus fertilization level (low P, adequate P, high P)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract EVERY AMF species x crop x P level combination separately
3. If multiple AMF species tested, extract EACH vs the non-AMF control
5. Record AMF species and P fertilization level
6. Biomass outcomes acceptable when grain yield not reported
tc_confusion_warnings: In factorial AMF x P designs, extract each AMF vs non-AMF at matching P level
Sterilized soil control may behave differently from field soil - note if soil was sterilized
Some papers compare AMF species to each other - we want each vs the NON-AMF control
Root colonization % is NOT the yield outcome - extract yield/biomass as the primary outcome

search.seed_papers_description: Hoeksema et al. 2010 (Ecology Letters, major meta-analysis), Berruti et al. 2016 (review of AMF in agriculture), Lekberg & Koide 2005

inclusion_criteria: Experiment comparing AMF-inoculated vs non-inoculated plants
Reports yield or biomass data (numeric means)
exclusion_criteria: Only wild/forest species with no agricultural relevance
Only root colonization data without yield/biomass

published_pooled_effect.notes: Overall +23% plant biomass; C4 grasses +57%, forbs +32%, C3 grasses +14%, woody plants +18%; Low P: larger effect; High P: reduced effect
